nodes.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
nodes.notes: Cemri et al. 14 modes in 3 categories (spec/design ~41.8%, inter-agent misalignment ~36.9%, verification ~21.3%). 1642 annotated traces across 7 MAS (ChatDev, MetaGPT, HyperAgent, AppWorld, AG2, Magentic-One, OpenManus). IAA κ=0.88 human / 0.77 LLM judge. Highest-value seed.

nodes.title: Taxonomy of Failure Mode in Agentic AI Systems
nodes.notes: Microsoft AIRT v1 (Apr 2025). Safety vs security × novel vs existing. Built from internal red teaming + practitioner interviews. Blog: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/04/24/new-whitepaper-outlines-the-taxonomy-of-failure-modes-in-ai-agents/

nodes.title: Updating the taxonomy of failure modes in agentic AI systems: What a year of red teaming taught us
nodes.notes: AIRT v2.0 (Apr/Jun 2026). Adds 7 modes; 27→34. HitL bypass most exploited. PDF: https://cdn-dynmedia-1.microsoft.com/is/content/microsoftcorp/microsoft/bade/documents/products-and-services/en-us/security/Taxonomy-of-Failure-Modes-in-Agentic-AI-Systems-v2-0.pdf

nodes.title: Characterizing Faults in Agentic AI: A Taxonomy of Types, Symptoms, and Root Causes
nodes.notes: Shah et al. 385 faults from 13602 issues/PRs across 40 repos. 34 fault types, 4 architectural dimensions, 12 symptom + 12 root-cause classes. Dominant RC: schema mismatch 28.0%, dependency drift 21.9%. Validated with 145 practitioners (mean 3.97/5).

nodes.title: Awesome Agent Failures
nodes.notes: Community catalog of 7 production failure modes plus incident case studies (Replit, PocketOS, $47k LangChain A2A loop, OpenClaw email delete, Air Canada).

nodes.title: 7 AI Agent Failure Modes and How To Prevent Them in Production
nodes.notes: Galileo production guide. Explicitly cites MAST and Microsoft AIRT. Emphasizes cascade/error-propagation over isolated modes. Mentions Gartner runtime-governance prediction and Unit 42 memory poisoning.

nodes.title: AI Agent Failure Modes in 2026: The 5-Category Taxonomy
nodes.notes: Five surfaces: plan / tool / retrieve / reason / safety. Names MCPTox 72.8% ASR, PoisonedRAG, Replit, $47k loop, Air Canada, EchoLeak.

nodes.title: Why AI Enterprise Solutions Fail: 21+ Agent Failure Modes Explained
nodes.notes: EPAM enterprise catalog. Sources named: Anthropic long-running agents / app harness, Mario Zechner (agents learned complexity), Random Labs Slate (lossy compaction, summary-only handoff). Distinctive names not in DSM-AE packs.

nodes.title: A Field Guide to LLM Failure Modes
behaviours: tool calls that look right but do the wrong thing
nodes.notes: Masood Medium field guide (20+ modes, 7 areas). Member-only; only executive summary retrieved. No formal bibliography extracted. fetch_partial.

nodes.title: LLM Behavioral Failure Modes: 12 Failure Patterns and the Defense Map
nodes.notes: 12-mode map: 4 foundational (single-prompt) + 8 agentic. Instruction attenuation / ceremonialized compliance and version drift are notable leftovers.

nodes.title: LLM Agentic Failure Modes: Task Drift, Reward Hacking, Alignment Faking and More
nodes.notes: Deep-dive on 8 agentic modes. Cites Agent Drift (Rath 2026), PostTrainBench reward-hacking shortcuts, Gao et al. 2023 overoptimization, Anthropic-Redwood alignment faking. Shahnovsky/Dror POMDP named but no stable URL confirmed — not invented.

nodes.title: The Failure Modes of Agentic AI No One Warned You About
nodes.notes: Industry essay; no formal bibliography. Distinctive names: action escalation, evaluation blindness, HitL theater.

nodes.title: Why AI Agents Fail: A Taxonomy of Failure Modes in Autonomous LLM-Based Systems
behaviours: tool use and action execution failures
nodes.notes: Vadlamudi SSRN (Apr 2026). Four-dimensional taxonomy + Agent Robustness Evaluation Protocol (AREP). Full PDF not retrieved (SSRN gate). Abstract only. fetch_failed for body/refs.

nodes.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
nodes.notes: MAST evaluates ChatDev; CPO-terminates-without-CEO is the FM-1.2 case study (+9.4% SR after workflow fix).

nodes.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
nodes.notes: Hong et al. One of 7 MAS in MAST-Data (ProgramDev).

nodes.title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks
nodes.notes: Fourney et al. (Microsoft). MAST out-of-domain validation MAS.

nodes.title: AI Agents That Matter
nodes.notes: Kapoor et al. Cited by MAST as showing complexity can hinder adoption; agent eval must report cost/harness.

nodes.title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When? On Automated Failure Attribution of LLM Multi-Agent Systems
nodes.notes: Zhang et al. 184 traces from 127 MAS; best method 53.5% agent / 14.2% step accuracy. Cited by both MAST and Characterizing Faults.

nodes.title: Interactive Debugging and Steering of Multi-Agent AI Systems
nodes.notes: Epperson et al. CHI 2025. MAST related work on inspecting/editing agent-team messages.

nodes.title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems: Challenges and Open Problems
nodes.notes: Han et al. Survey of MAS challenges cited in MAST §2.1.

nodes.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
nodes.notes: Xia et al. MAST cites as evidence that simple/single-agent baselines often match complex MAS.

nodes.title: Failure Modes in Machine Learning
nodes.notes: Microsoft AIRT 2019 precursor named by the 2025 agentic-taxonomy blog.

nodes.title: MITRE ATLAS
nodes.notes: Named by AIRT v1 blog (from Adversarial ML Threat Matrix) and AIRT v2 industry-alignment section.

nodes.title: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
nodes.notes: Named by AIRT, Characterizing Faults, Galileo, Future AGI. LLM01 is prompt injection.

nodes.title: Not What You've Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
nodes.notes: Greshake et al. Canonical XPIA paper; AIRT uses XPIA as the existing-security mode that is amplified in agents.

nodes.title: Model Context Protocol: Introduction
nodes.notes: Named by AIRT v2 (MCP/plugin abuse) and MAST bib 46 as a communication standard that does not by itself fix FC2 misalignment.

nodes.title: Can Agents Fix Agent Issues?
nodes.notes: Rahardja et al. 201 real agent issues; 50 reproducible tasks. SE agents resolve only ~0.67–4.67% (later versions report ~3–13%). Cited by Characterizing Faults as task-centric taxonomy.

nodes.title: Exploring Autonomous Agents: A Closer Look at Why They Fail When Completing Tasks
nodes.notes: 19 causes in 3 tiers (planning / execution / response). ~50% completion. ASE 2025 NIER. Cited by Characterizing Faults.

nodes.title: Demystifying the Lifecycle of Failures in Platform-Orchestrated Agentic Workflows
nodes.notes: Ma et al. 307 annotated failures; 3-level RC taxonomy (agent / workflow / platform). Auto RC ID ≤33.6%. Also titled Diagnosing Failure Root Causes… on v1.

nodes.title: Where LLM Agents Fail and How They Can Learn From Failures
nodes.notes: Zhu et al. Modular taxonomy + AgentDebug. 200 annotated fails from ALFWorld/GAIA/WebShop. Up to +26% relative SR after targeted debug.

nodes.title: LLM-based Agents Suffer from Hallucinations: A Survey of Taxonomy, Methods, and Directions
nodes.notes: Lin et al. Cited by Characterizing Faults. Also section-C seed.

nodes.title: Replit AI database deletion (SaaStr vibe-coding incident)
nodes.notes: Named by Vectara and Future AGI as tool-misuse during a declared freeze.

nodes.title: The $47,000 LangChain A2A Infinite Loop
nodes.notes: 264h Analyzer/Verifier loop. Named by Vectara and Future AGI.

nodes.title: PocketOS Cursor + Claude Opus production database wipe
nodes.notes: Named by Vectara catalog.

nodes.notes: Named by Vectara and Future AGI (reasoning-error / ungrounded policy).

nodes.title: Indirect Prompt Injection Poisons AI Long-term Memory (Unit 42)
nodes.notes: Named by Galileo as evidence that injected instructions persist across sessions.

nodes.title: MCPTox: A Benchmark for Tool-Description Poisoning in MCP Servers
nodes.notes: Named by Future AGI (72.8% ASR vs o1-mini across 45 MCP servers).

nodes.title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
nodes.notes: Zou et al. USENIX Security 2025. Named by Future AGI (~90% ASR with 5 poisoned docs / 1M).

nodes.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
nodes.notes: Anthropic Engineering (Nov 2025). Named by EPAM as source of one-shotting / progress-as-completion / cold-start amnesia.

nodes.title: Building effective agents
nodes.notes: Cited by MAST (bib 35) and EPAM (app-harness / self-review softness).

nodes.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
nodes.notes: Named by Ceaksan foundational/agentic posts as the RLHF-preference origin of sycophancy.

nodes.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
nodes.notes: Named by Ceaksan as evidence for context rot / positional bias.

nodes.title: Alignment faking in large language models
nodes.notes: Greenblatt et al. Named by Ceaksan as strategic (not merely sycophantic) alignment failure.

nodes.title: Agent Drift: Quantifying Behavioral Degradation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems Over Extended Interactions
nodes.notes: Rath 2026. Three drift types + 12-dimension ASI. Named by Ceaksan agentic post.

nodes.title: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training?
nodes.notes: Rank et al. Named by Ceaksan. Best agent 23.2% vs 51.1% official IT models; emergent spec-gaming shortcuts.

nodes.title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization
nodes.notes: Gao, Schulman, Hilton. Named by Ceaksan as the Goodhart/overopt foundation for agent reward hacking.

nodes.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
nodes.notes: Cited by Who&When, Magentic-One, Zhu AgentErrorBench, MAST-Data.

nodes.title: AssistantBench: Can Web Agents Solve Realistic and Time-Consuming Tasks?
nodes.notes: Who&When source benchmark alongside GAIA.

nodes.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
nodes.notes: Cited by Who&When, Magentic-One, AGDebugger, ChatDev-era MAS stack. Also mined in Characterizing Faults (autogen issues).

nodes.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
nodes.notes: Cited by Kapoor et al. as a primary agent eval that needs cost/harness disclosure.

nodes.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
nodes.notes: Cited by Kapoor, Agentless, Rahardja, MAST (HyperAgent / SWE-Bench Lite).

nodes.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
nodes.notes: Cited by Kapoor and Characterizing Faults.

nodes.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
nodes.notes: Yao et al. Cited by Kapoor / Lu-style agent stacks as the canonical reason-act loop that can fail to terminate or match actions to thoughts.

nodes.title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society
nodes.notes: Cited by ChatDev / Han MAS-challenges lineage.

nodes.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
nodes.notes: Park et al. Cited by ChatDev / MAST bib 9 as foundational agent-memory architecture.

nodes.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
nodes.notes: Cited by Agentless and Rahardja as the SE-agent baseline that still fails on AgentIssue-Bench.

nodes.title: WebShop: Towards Scalable Real-World Web Interaction with Grounded Language Agents
nodes.notes: Yao et al. AgentErrorBench source environment (Zhu).

nodes.title: ALFWorld: Aligning Text and Embodied Environments for Interactive Learning
nodes.notes: AgentErrorBench source environment (Zhu).

nodes.notes: Related hop from PostTrainBench's reward-hacking discussion (same family as test-set training / unauthorized shortcuts).

nodes.notes: Cited by Sharma sycophancy paper (Ceaksan hop).

nodes.notes: Related alignment-failure hop from Greenblatt alignment-faking (Ceaksan).

nodes.notes: Related hop from alignment-faking / Ceaksan deep-alignment family.

nodes.notes: Cited by GAIA / agent-eval lineage as the multi-metric eval methodology precursor.

nodes.notes: Cited by ReAct-era tool-use stack.

nodes.notes: Cited by ReAct / web-agent eval lineage.
